newsitem.title: USA: AMA backs partial birth abortion ban.
newsitem.headline: AMA backs partial birth abortion ban.

text.p: The chief sponsor of the so-called partial birth abortion ban announced Monday that he had won the backing of the American Medical Association, an influential doctors' professional body.
The ban, sponsored by Pennsylvania Republican Rick Santorum, is expected to face a Senate vote Tuesday.

Santorum has enough votes to pass the ban, but is still trying to win over five more votes needed to withstand a promised veto by President Bill Clinton. The measure passed the House of Representatives by a veto-proof majority.
He released a letter in which the AMA confirmed it supported the ban.

To win AMA backing, Santorum added a change to the bill so that a doctor who performed the procedure would face a review by a state medical board before any criminal proceedings could take place and the board's findings would be admissible in court.

"The president might have to look very long and hard about whether he wants to veto this," Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, who backs the ban on the procedure, also known as dilation and evacuation, said earlier in the day.

An anti-abortion activist said the AMA directly may not swing votes but would undercut the argument made by Clinton and other opponents of the ban that exemptions were needed to protect the health of a pregnant woman. The bill only allows the procedure to save the life of a woman.
The American College of Obstretricians and Gynecologists has opposed the ban, saying there can be rare health situations when it is the best medical option.
